Hi Jacqueline — thanks for the context and the sheet. Short answers up front, then a recommended path.

Options for reserved pool increases:
- Step increments: +4, +8, +16 GPUs (A100-eq); standard lead time 14 days for +4/+8, 30 days for +16+ depending on regional capacity.
- Price tiers: incremental discount applies at >20 GPUs or >24/7 throughput SLAs. We'll include a tiered rate schedule in the quote.

Overage/fallback approaches we offer:
1) On-demand routing (preferred by most customers):
   - Excess traffic routes to Redwood hosted fleet; billed at overage per-token rate.
   - Latency: additive network hop but we keep p95 latencies within ~1.1–1.5x the reserved pool baseline depending on region and model size.
   - SLA: reserved pool performance SLA applies to committed capacity; hosted overage uses best-effort with prioritized routing for enterprise deals.

2) Hard cap (throttle):
   - No routing to hosted fleet once reserved capacity is exhausted; additional requests are queued/throttled or receive a 429.
   - Guarantees upper-bound spend but increases error rates and perceived downtime.

Recommended path for CloudScale based on your growth: expand to a 20 GPU reserved pool (adds +8), enable on-demand routing for burst with a monthly hard spend cap that you can set (e.g., $30k/mo) to guard budgeting. That gives you headroom, keeps customer experience intact, and limits upside spend.

If that sounds reasonable I'll loop in Marissa (SE) to validate throughput numbers and Karthik for contractual language around spend caps + SLA carve-outs. Also can attach a draft SOW with pricing.

—Dev

Hi all — ran the numbers against their traffic profile. Short summary and next steps below.

Throughput & sizing notes:
- Customer telemetry indicates heavy short-chat sessions and a growing batch-embedding job overnight. Peak steady-state RPS today ~32 req/s; p50 token lengths ~240, p95 ~640.
- Conservative guardrails suggest +8 GPUs (20 total) will move p95 latency back to sub-200ms for interactive flows at your target concurrency (assuming 8-worker pooling per GPU). For embedding batches we recommend a scheduled batch slot to avoid contention (we can reserve a nightly slot in the dedicated pool).

Latency impact for on-demand routing:
- We estimate hosted overage routing will add ~60–120ms at p95 for your region/model mix (network + queueing). For large embedding jobs (long sequences) the delta can be larger; recommend redirecting those to a batched pathway.

Proposed contractual mechanics for spend cap:
- Soft cap: alerting at 70/85/100% of monthly overage budget, failover behavior is configurable (auto-throttle vs continue and bill).
- Hard spend cap option: once monthly overage spend reaches cap, further overage traffic is either throttled (429) or routed to a degraded model tier with explicit opt-in; this incurs a lower per-token discount and may increase latency.
- Billing flow: overage tracked daily; invoice includes reserved line item + overage line item; if hard cap hits, invoice reflects capped overage and a one-time admin block event in audit logs.

Attached: redwood-throughput-estimate-v2.pdf (technical calc) and SOW draft (SOW-draft-CloudScale-2027.docx). Please review redlines and confirm whether CloudScale wants nightly embedding reserved slots (recommended) or prefer burst to hosted fleet.

—Marissa
